paragraphs.source_en:
diverse for brief summary; the notes which follow attempt to give at least an indication of the
variety and density of the play’s cultural reference. Paradise Lost is a pervasive influence, as is
the Bible; Shakespeare, Spenser, Dante, Lucretius and Virgil are all central, and the Greek trage-
dians. Plato and Platonic ideas are important, including their mediation in many classical and
Renaissance sources. There are marked local influences from many of S.’s contemporaries, par-
ticularly Byron, Hunt, Coleridge, Peacock, and Godwin. The play also makes some coded ref-
erence to S.’s immediate circle and biographical circumstances; e.g. Mercury suggests Byron’s
cynical worldliness as S. may recently have experienced it directly in Venice in the late summer
of 1818; Prometheus, Asia and Proteus in III iii equate with S., Mary and Godwin; sometimes
Panthea and Ione may suggest Mary and Claire Clairmont (see also notes to III i 19, III iii 64–8).
